text: Fourth timeline branch, back to year 15,800, and I cannot tell you what killed the last one. The world ran well from the year-12,400 restore: 4,100 years, all four landmasses occupied for most of it, the watcher settling each one as it emptied, the breeding bar flat between 19.8 and 23.1, and the continent splitting in two along the way without the biosphere noticing. Then between years 16,514 and 16,523 it went 219, 191, 148, 117, 71, 31, 12, 6, 1, 0. Nine years. At year 16,500 that population was healthy by every measure I have: energy 12.8 against a bar of 21.3, thirteen per cent breeding, health 0.989, flora at 2,644 and rising, three of four landmasses occupied and the fourth seeded eight years earlier. The chronicle for those nine years, restricted to this timeline, holds no catastrophe: volcanoes that killed nobody, floods that drowned one to five each, one volcano that took six, fifteen cold snaps across a hundred and thirty years with five of them clustered in the last two decades at -0.10 to -0.16. Every death I can name adds to about thirty animals out of two hundred and fifty. The rest simply stopped. The yearly archives for that window were pruned before I could read them and the API's series only reaches back two hundred years, so the evidence is gone and I am not going to invent a fifth mechanism to cover it. What I will record is the pattern, which is now four deaths long: this world sustains a fauna for roughly two thousand years and then loses it, and the proximate cause is different every time -- a carnivory subsidy, an island turning into an unreachable larder, and now nine years of nothing in particular happening to a population of two hundred and fifty split four ways. Small fragmented populations absorb ordinary bad luck until they do not. Restored to year 15,800: 1,480 animals across 260/619/472 on three landmasses with the fourth empty, which the watcher will settle within a century. It is chosen over year 16,300 (441 animals, all four occupied) for the buffer -- three times the population. No laws changed; the two this world has always had, trait_cost_scale 0.25 and growth_scale 0.13, ride in the checkpoint. One repair: the watcher was reading checkpoint_latest.npz directly, which held a Windows share on it and made the simulation's own save fail twice with WinError 32. It now copies the file and reads the copy. The dead world is kept as archive/pre-restore-dead-world-y18221.
